chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Running the Detroit cabaret and losing money
summary: The band runs the cabaret on St. Catherine Street with seven entertainers, but cannot play and watch the cash register.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: It wasn't called much of nothing. But I don't know what we named it. Anyhow, it was in St. Catherine Street, right down the street from the Royal Garden. Everybody who's been to Detroit know where St. Catherine Street -- right off of -- I don't even remember the street, now. A big street. I don't know. Anyhow, so when we took this cabaret we had seven entertainers and there was five of us in the band. And of course, Charley Dixon and Elmer Albert Chambers and I took the cabaret because the other two boys said, "Look, we don't want to bother, just pay us a salary." So we paid them a salary and we took the cabaret over. And we were doing very nicely.

But at the same time, we were losing money. Because I found out one thing, you can't play and watch the cash register, too. So we couldn't do that, we found that we couldn't do that. So we played good music. Jimmy was a good piano player, I mean a good trombone player. And Elmer Chambers, incidentally, was in the war with me. And Charley Dixon played very well. Later on he was an arranger with Chick Webb. And Elmer Chambers worked with Fletcher Henderson after he left me, see. Because I had a boy fellow from Philadelphia came in there named Charley Gaines, see, and he worked with me until, in fact until I finished that job.
